saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting in SAML login flows.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and should not be flagged as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: Userinfo and token claims are returned only when corresponding scopes were granted.
saml.note: Missing email/profile/roles claims without requesting the matching scopes is expected behavior.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token as requested_token_type, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows the documented RFC 8693 handling; do not use that field as a bearer token.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default for many applications.
saml.note: Opaque tokens require introspection or userinfo rather than local JWT parsing; this is not a bug.

saml.description: SAML endpoint errors can be returned with HTTP 200 while the SAML payload carries a failure StatusCode.
saml.note: A 200 response from SAML endpoints is not sufficient evidence of successful authentication.

saml.description: ZITADEL commonly issues opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Tests must use userinfo or introspection rather than local JWT parsing unless JWT access tokens were explicitly requested/configured.

saml.description: ZITADEL can intentionally link an external SAML identity to an existing local account, either manually or automatically depending on provider settings.
saml.note: Identity merges are not automatically bugs; only unexpected merges outside configured linking behavior should be flagged.

saml.description: If organization-specific settings override defaults, the correct external IdP is only selected when the auth request carries the organization scope.
saml.note: Wrong IdP selection without org scope is expected configuration behavior, not a broker flaw.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML login against ZITADEL as the broker/SP path; a valid SAML test must begin with an SP-generated request and preserve the matching request context (for example InResponseTo via the initiated flow).

For SAML broker tests against ZITADEL Login V2, user creation can fail unless required user fields are mapped from upstream SAML attributes. The fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream assertion provides required attributes and/or an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent populates username, given name, family name, and email before treating login failure as a security rejection.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' on the relevant instance or organization before any SAML broker login test; otherwise login failures are policy failures, not protocol-security rejections.

If organization-specific settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default settings and a different IdP/login policy than intended, causing false I3/I4/I5 results.

To force direct redirection to a specific external identity provider during OIDC-wrapped SAML broker tests, include reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}. Without it, UI/provider selection and domain discovery may change which upstream IdP is used, invalidating flow-coherence tests.

The OIDC token endpoint's audience parameter in token exchange is restrictive: audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. For I5 audience-binding tests, do not request a brand-new audience and interpret rejection as correct behavior; only test whether ZITADEL improperly accepts audiences outside that subset.
The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target behavior. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource for I5 authorization-binding tests on ZITADEL.

ZITADEL token exchange supports only specific token-type combinations. In particular, refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token or actor_token; JWT subject_token is only allowed as a self-signed JWT in combination with a valid actor_token; user_id subject_token is only allowed in combination with actor_token. The fuzzer MUST stay within these documented combinations or treat failures as setup errors.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that access_token value as a bearer API credential or as a successful session token for follow-up API calls.

For I5 token-exchange scope escalation tests, ZITADEL may return scopes that differ from the requested scope after validation. The oracle MUST compare the returned scope and resulting claims, not just whether the request was syntactically accepted.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT-based client authentication to /oauth/v2/token (private_key_jwt or JWT profile), iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls; otherwise failures are malformed-client-auth failures, not freshness enforcement findings.

ZITADEL userinfo and introspection behavior depends on granted scopes. For verify_granted_identity and I4/I5 checks, the fuzzer MUST request the necessary scopes (for example profile, email, reserved role scopes) during authorization or token exchange; absent claims due to missing scope are by design and not evidence of identity/authorization loss.

The introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. For any verification strategy using introspection, the fuzzer MUST ensure the introspecting client is in the token audience; otherwise inactive/401 results are expected and not token invalidity.

SAML endpoint errors may be conveyed with HTTP 200 and an error StatusCode in the SAML payload. The fuzzer MUST NOT rely on HTTP status alone when evaluating SAML protocol success/failure on /saml/v2/SSO-style flows.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow first and bind any forged SAMLResponse to the issued request/intent; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML broker tests, login success is not obtained directly from a SAML ACS that returns a bearer token. The correct sequence is: start OIDC authorization at /oauth/v2/authorize, follow the external IdP/SAML path, finalize the SAML request, then exchange the returned authorization code at /oauth/v2/token. Do NOT expect saml_login itself to return the session bearer token.

When testing SAML provider selection for organization-specific IdPs, the authorization request SHOULD include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may use default settings and the expected external IdP button/redirect may not appear, causing false negatives in SAML broker tests.

To force direct redirect to a specific external IdP during OIDC login, use the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}. Without this scope, ZITADEL may present a chooser UI or apply domain discovery, which can invalidate flow-coherence assumptions in automated SAML tests.

External IdP login must be allowed by login policy. The fuzzer MUST ensure 'External Login allowed' is enabled before running SAML broker tests; otherwise login failures are policy failures, not SAML validation failures.

For Login V2 SAML identity brokering, user creation can fail unless required user fields are mapped from SAML attributes via an Action on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST provision attribute mapping or use identities whose required fields are already satisfiable; otherwise SAML login failures may be onboarding failures rather than security enforcement.

SAML SSO endpoint errors may still return HTTP 200 with failure encoded in SAML StatusCode. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML endpoints as success by itself; it must inspect downstream flow outcome (redirect/code issuance or SAML status) to distinguish accepted vs rejected assertions.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, documentation only states best practices and metadata/certificate exchange; it does not document insecure defaults such as skipping signature validation when provider settings are omitted. The fuzzer SHOULD treat acceptance of attacker-signed assertions as a finding only when the configured IdP trust material should have enabled verification, and avoid assuming undocumented default flags like validateSignature or wantAssertionsSigned exist in ZITADEL docs.

For I2 freshness tests on OIDC tokens obtained after SAML login, include a control login using a valid baseline flow. Token endpoint and userinfo failures can stem from client configuration, missing org scope, or disabled external login; without a control, attack-token rejection is ambiguous.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target audience; otherwise rejection is expected behavior, not a vulnerability.
Token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target behavior. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns that ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use such a returned value as a bearer session token for verification calls.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For token-exchange freshness or impersonation tests, expired-ID-token rejection is by design and not evidence of broader replay protection beyond documented checks.

For impersonation-style token exchange tests, actor_token is optional syntactically but required for subject_token_type jwt and urn:zitadel:params:oauth:token-type:user_id. The fuzzer MUST include a valid actor_token with impersonation permission for these cases; otherwise rejection is expected.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange, ZITADEL may return scopes different from the requested scope after validation. The fuzzer MUST compare the returned scope field and resulting claims, not just whether the request was accepted.

For introspection- or userinfo-based verification, opaque access tokens are normal in ZITADEL. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume JWT structure in session_token after code exchange or token exchange unless requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt or the application is configured for JWT access tokens.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate a flow first and obtain a SAML request / request ID before attempting saml_login; unsolicited IdP-initiated SAMLResponse tests are invalid on this platform.

For brokered SAML login into ZITADEL Login V2, user creation fails unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes. The fuzzer MUST configure an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent or otherwise ensure required attributes (email, first name, last name, username) are populated before treating login failure as a security result.

When testing organization-scoped external IdPs, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may use default settings and not the organization-specific SAML provider, causing false negatives or wrong-provider routing.

To force direct redirect to a specific external IdP, the fuzzer SHOULD include scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}. Without this scope, login UI selection and domain discovery may alter which upstream IdP is used, invalidating SAML-specific attack setup.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on protocol/authentication errors; failure is encoded inside the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML exchanges as success by itself.

For I1 SAML issuer-validation tests, the configured SAML provider metadata/entity ID must be present and trusted. If the provider is created from incomplete or placeholder metadata, issuer validation results are meaningless because trust material is not fully established.

For I2 replay tests on SAML assertions, ZITADEL documentation states SAML best practice requires historical cache / duplicate ID rejection, but the provided docs do not expose a replay-cache configuration parameter. The fuzzer SHOULD run same-assertion-ID replay and OneTimeUse replay as behavioral tests and interpret success on first submission as control before judging second submission.

For I3 config-change tests involving external IdPs, enabling/disabling or relinking an IdP in login policy legitimately changes future logins. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of equivalent requests before and after the change, not flag the administrative change itself as a bug.

For I4 identity-binding tests, ZITADEL may create or link users based on external IdP information and configured linking options. The fuzzer MUST control whether automatic creation/linking is enabled; otherwise cross-user merge findings may reflect configured account-linking behavior rather than an unintended collision.

For I4 SAML email-binding-collision and cross-protocol-merge tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish between first-time account creation, manual/automatic linking, and existing linked identities. ZITADEL explicitly supports linking external identities to existing accounts, so merges are only suspicious when they occur without the configured linking criteria/flow.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, audience in token exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. The fuzzer must first obtain a control token whose audience already contains the target project/application; otherwise rejection is expected behavior, not a vulnerability.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope may differ from input scope, but ZITADEL validates and may return a reduced final scope in the response. The fuzzer MUST compare granted response scope/claims, not merely requested scope, when deciding whether escalation occurred.

For I5 token exchange resource-indicator tests, the resource parameter is currently unsupported and always results in invalid_target behavior. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat resource-related failures as audience-binding security findings.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT client assertions or JWT profile grants, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls; otherwise failures may be due to malformed client authentication rather than freshness enforcement.
